answers.question: What weakness did we find?
sentences: 60 of 62 night validation frames carry at least one baseline miss.

answers.question: What data did we add?
sentences: `graph_rate_night` mined 1,500 frames across 368 scenes, 31% at night — random covered 501 scenes at 13% night; similarity mining covered 219 scenes at 0% night.
Visual similarity alone concentrated on daytime appearance (0% night); the graph + night-floor arm explicitly preserved night coverage.

answers.question: Did the model improve?
sentences: Night mAP50-95 0.1667 → 0.1768 (+0.0101) on the held-out split.
The best overall arm is `graph` (+0.0344); the night arm trades overall gain for night gain.

answers.question: What failed along the way?
sentences: Weak (VLM-verified) labels kept 18.2% of the ground-truth gain for the `random` pair: 49.7% was lost with the frames the verifier dropped, 32.1% to label noise on the ones it kept.
The verifier kept sparse frames: 3.87 vs 7.61 GT boxes per accepted vs rejected frame (random).
`weak_graph_rate_night` is the worst night result of the 13 arms (-0.0262).
The hero frame's pedestrian recovery is a low-confidence claim (conf 0.135) — counted as a hit by the matching rule, not a confident detection.

closing_thesis: Instead of blindly retraining the model, the system diagnoses where it fails, finds the data that can address the weakness, and measures whether the intervention actually works.
headline: Closed the loop: weakness → targeted data → measurable improvement
